messages:
rachel: Noticed an increase in host-side CPU for short streaming requests after the selector+batching rollout. Cropped pprof shows selector scoring and repeated kv lookups.
omar: timeframe + region?
rachel: started 2026-03-24T01:12 UTC, observed in ap-southeast-1 and us-west-2 during multiplex bursts.
perfbot: deploy event: selector-batching-2026-03-24 by @ci-bot -> canary 20% -> promoted 01:10
sylvie: top from a 30s CPU sample (sanitized):
```
# top 8
16.4% kernel_selector::score_candidates
13.0% kv_cache::lookup
10.2% tokenize::scan_ascii_fastpath
8.7% http2::hpack_decode
7.5% parse_proto_frame
6.0% batch_coordinator::record_chunk
5.8% writev::flush
4.1% sched::wake
```
omar: kernel_selector scoring that high implies it's being invoked multiple times per request. batching change probably rescores per chunk.
rachel: selector_call_count metric jumped from ~1.1 to ~4.2 on 40-80 token inputs. KV miss-rate +14%.
ops: kv keys look like they include variant_stamp; maybe selector produced ephemeral variant_ids leading to churn.
sylvie: two hypotheses: 1) batching-vX rescores per chunk (O(chunks)) 2) selector now computes richer features on host (seq-length, perf-model-sim) instead of sidecar. both increase CPU.
omar: quick mitigations: - memoize selector per (route, model, quant_profile, short=true) - add fastpath: if token_count<96 reuse last selection - make variant_id stable (remove ephemeral salt) - increase batching window by ~2ms to reduce chunk churn
rachel: can we run a wrk reproduction? I can run a jittered multiplex script against canary.
ops: share wrk script: `wrk -t6 -c150 -d60s --latency \'lua_short_stream.lua\' http://ingress:8080/v1/stream` where lua sends 30-70 token prompts and drains streaming frames.
sylvie: also check HPACK decode counts. small fragmented frames increase hpack decoding per-request which amplifies parse cost. add metric `hpack_decodes_per_request`.
perfbot: CI perf test failed for 50-token scenario by +7.1% CPU after rollout.
omar: plan: 1) roll canary back to pre-rollout binary for 20% traffic 2) implement selector memo + fastpath + stable variant id 3) add telemetry: selector_calls_per_request, kv_evictions_per_minute, hpack_decodes_per_request 4) run wrk before/after and collect pprofs and flamegraphs
rachel: initiating rollback now.
ci-bot: rollback started at 01:27 by @rachel (selector-batching revert) -> canary 20% -> progress ok
ops: after rollback initial wrk shows CPU back to baseline in canary; will run longer test to be sure.
sylvie: follow-ups for eng-runtime: - make scorer idempotent and cheap for short inputs - ensure selector is executed at most once per request when possible - audit kv key derivation to exclude ephemeral fields - add regression perf-tests for 0-128 token path
omar: I'll open a ticket with the perf diffs and assign. Also add a unit test that asserts selector_calls_for_short_input == 1.
rachel: thanks all. once patches land we'll canary the optimized selector and watch selector_calls_per_request and kv_eviction metrics closely. :thumbsup:
